text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- The cabinet gave greater powers to election tribunals to disbar an elected member from the assembly if a petition challenging his election is pending against him.

- The ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) and the Pakistan Peoples Party (Shaheed Bhutto) have reached an electoral understanding for national and provincial assembly seats in the southern province of Sindh.
- The Pakistan Muslim League has agreed on seat adjustment with one of its splinter factions in Sindh province.
- The election campaign of deposed prime minister Benazir Bhutto got a new boost when her mother Nusrat Bhutto made her first appearance at a rally in her hometown of Larkana.
- The counsel for President Farooq Leghari told the Supreme Court he could not get records of extra-judicial killings in Karachi.
- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan in a circular has laid down new guidelines for banks to calculate their capital adequacy requirement on the basis of risk-weighted assets.
- The Pakistan Cotton Ginners Association has asked the state-run Cotton Export Corporation to buy an estimated two million 375-lb bales of unsold cotton stocked in ginneries.
BUSINESS RECORDER

- A new banking authority, Resolution Trust Corporation of Pakistan (RTCP), has been established with an authorised capital of 200 billion rupees. RTCP would be responsible for cleansing the infected portfolios, recovery and rescheduling of loans, and privatisation of state-run banks and financial institutions.
- With the arrival of 315,000 tonnes of imported wheat, a shortage at flour mills in Sindh province will be over in the next few days.
- The state-run Pakistan International Airline Corporation plans to expand its fleet and replace some of its aircraft to cope with growing passenger traffic, a comapny official said.
FINANCIAL POST
- The cabinet approved a one-time increase of 5.9 percent in electricity tariffs applicable for February only.
- The cabinet has decided to replace one-, two- and five-rupee denomination notes with coins.
THE NEWS
- President Farooq Leghari said he might resign on moral grounds if the Supreme Court restores the government of Benazir Bhutto which he dismissed on November 5.
- The government has set up a Electronic Media Regulatory Authority to issue licences to operators of private radio and television channels and end monopolies in this sector.
--Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
